turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning

Scanning the training data, the highest-Tc superconductors are all cuprates: Bi2Sr2Ca1Cu2O10 (Tc=110), Tl0.5Pb0.5Ba1.6Sr0.4Ca2Cu3O (Tc=120.2), Ba2Ca2Cu3O (Tc=126), Hg1Ba2Ca2Cu3O8 (Tc=132), and the closest slightly-lower example Tl1Sr2Sr0.5Eu0.5Cu2O7 (Tc=71.0).

The target Tc=90 K sits almost exactly between the 71 K (Tl-cuprate) and 110 K (Bi-2212) data points, both of which belong to the Bi/Tl-based layered cuprate family (Sr, Ca, Cu, O as the core elements, with a heavy cation—Bi, Tl, or Pb—providing the charge-balancing layer). This is consistent with real-world superconductivity data, where the classic Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8 ("Bi-2212") phase has an experimentally well-known Tc ≈ 85–95 K, i.e., almost exactly the target value.

I therefore build the composition directly from the Bi-2212 stoichiometry (Bi2Sr2Ca1Cu2O8), normalizing to fractional units (dividing by the total atom count = 2+2+1+2+8 = 15):

- Bi: 2/15 = 0.133333  (within [0, 0.521978])
- Sr: 2/15 = 0.133333  (within [0, 0.285714])
- Ca: 1/15 = 0.066667  (within [0, 0.272727])
- Cu: 2/15 = 0.133333  (within [0, 0.454545])
- O: 8/15 = 0.533333   (within [0, 0.697674])

This composition is structurally identical to the Bi2Sr2Ca1Cu2O10 training example (Tc=110) but with a slightly reduced oxygen content (8 vs 10 formula units), which physically corresponds to reduced hole-doping and a lower, more optimally-doped Tc — consistent with shifting the value down from 110 K toward the ~90 K target, matching known Bi-2212 behavior.

All other elements are set to 0.
